Playbook.name: Linux — init (PID 1) Secret Dump via GDB - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: gdb was run via sudo (attaching to a process, e.g. PID 1, to dump memory/secrets). RECOVERED: USER_CMD captures sudo gdb with args (gdb attach to PID 1 requires root -> sudo).
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Dumping PID 1 memory extracts secrets held by init/systemd.

Assets.AssetType: Linux servers (core banking, app, DB - INTDOM)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: JCB Linux auditd does NOT audit execve (no EXECVE records, event.action:exec never occurs) or file paths. It DOES capture: USER_CMD (commands run via sudo, WITH process.args + auditd.log.AUID/UID user), SERVICE_STOP/START (auditd.log.unit), NETFILTER_CFG (firewall config), package events. These queries use those real records.

COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: USER_CMD captures only sudo-invoked commands - it misses actions taken when already root and non-sudo execution. Full coverage requires enabling auditd execve+file auditing (or Elastic Defend / ingesting the already-installed MDE-for-Linux device telemetry).

Signal.Name: init (PID 1) Secret Dump via GDB
Signal.Details: sudo command matching the behavior (auditd USER_CMD).

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Linux host where the command ran.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the init (pid 1) secret dump via gdb is malicious or a legitimate admin action, using the available sudo-command telemetry.

Step.name: Confirm the command via sudo (USER_CMD)
Step.Purpose: auditd USER_CMD records commands run via sudo with their arguments and the invoking user - the only command-with-args telemetry JCB Linux collects.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE auditd.log.record_type == "USER_CMD" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cmd = MV_CONCAT(process.args, " ") | WHERE cmd RLIKE ".*gdb.*" | KEEP @timestamp, auditd.log.AUID, auditd.log.UID, process.executable, cmd, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: sudo gdb by a non-developer AUID on a production host, especially attaching to PID 1 or a sensitive process (check the args), is memory-dump credential theft. Developer debugging on a dev host is benign.

Step.name: The user's other sudo commands (context)
Step.Purpose: The invoking user's other sudo activity separates an admin task from an attacker escalating.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE auditd.log.record_type == "USER_CMD" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cmd = MV_CONCAT(process.args, " ") | STATS commands = COUNT(*), samples = VALUES(cmd) BY auditd.log.AUID | SORT commands DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A known admin running maintenance via sudo differs from an unexpected user running credential/privilege commands. AUID is the real invoking user (login uid).

Node.Condition: sudo gdb attaching to a sensitive/init process by a non-developer on a production host.
The command was run by a known admin as part of documented maintenance.
Command observed but coverage-limited (may have run as root/non-sudo) and intent unclear - inspect the host.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-UC-CMD, INV-02-UC-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the admin/maintenance context; close as false_positive.
Inspect the host (full session, files touched); isolate if confirmed malicious; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A crash-analysis tool using gdb via sudo.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Inspect the host for the full command/session context (USER_CMD is sudo-only).

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture the session/files on-host; open IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: ENABLE auditd execve+file auditing OR ingest MDE-for-Linux device telemetry for full command/file coverage; redesign the detection to use USER_CMD/SERVICE_STOP/NETFILTER.

QualityChecks.Check: DETECTION DEFECT: the paired detection rule (EQL 'process where event.action:exec') CANNOT FIRE in JCB - auditd emits no execve events. REDESIGN the detection to key on auditd.log.record_type:USER_CMD with a process.args match (proven to capture this behavior when run via sudo). This playbook already uses that telemetry.

PARTIAL COVERAGE: USER_CMD captures sudo-invoked commands only; misses already-root and non-sudo execution. For full coverage enable auditd execve auditing or ingest MDE-for-Linux device telemetry (MDE/wdavdaemon is already installed on the Linux hosts).

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host inspected + contained; technique eradicated; peers swept.
